title: Saṅkalpa for the japa (midday)

words.gram: compound; final member dvāra, n., instr. sg. used adverbially
words.meaning: by way of the destruction of all the faults incurred
words.role: states the means: the rite works by removing faults

words.gram: compound ending in -artham (acc. sg. used adverbially, ‘for the sake of’)
words.meaning: for the pleasure of the glorious Supreme Lord
words.role: states the purpose of the act

words.meaning: the japa of the great mantra, the Gāyatrī, of the midday

samasa.vigraha: उपात्तानां समस्तानां दुरितानां क्षयः, तेन द्वारेण
samasa.meaning: by way of the destruction of all the faults that have been incurred
for the pleasure of the glorious Supreme Lord
the repetition of the great mantra, the Gāyatrī, at midday

translation.literal: By way of the destruction of all the faults incurred by me, for the pleasure of the glorious Supreme Lord, I shall perform the japa of the great mantra, the Gāyatrī, of the midday.
translation.readable: To remove every fault I have incurred, and for the pleasure of the Supreme Lord, I shall repeat the great mantra, the Gāyatrī, at midday.

meaning: The saṅkalpa, the statement of intent, for the Gāyatrī japa at midday. It names the means — the removal of all the faults one has incurred — and the purpose, the pleasure of the Supreme Lord, and then the act itself. The verbs are first person: the worshipper speaks for himself, and the formula is the same for every performer.
in_the_rite: Midday service, step japa-sankalpa, after śuklāmbaradharam and a prāṇāyāma.

notes.label: traditional
notes.text: A saṅkalpa is said with the breath held after the prāṇāyāma, or immediately after it; it names the act, the time, and the purpose. The Smārta form offers the act for the pleasure of the Supreme Lord (Parameśvara); Vaiṣṇava prayogas use other wording, which is outside this edition.
